title: The Real Reason We Trust People Who Look Like Us
hook: You instinctively trust people who look similar to you.

narration.text: You instinctively trust people who look similar to you.
This is called in-group bias, a natural human tendency.
Our brains prefer what is familiar and predictable.
Familiarity creates a sense of safety and belonging.
It means we often favour those within our own groups.
Recognising this bias helps us make fairer judgements.
Have you noticed this in your own interactions?

description: Discover why your brain naturally gravitates towards people who share similarities with you. Learn about in-group bias and how familiarity shapes our trust.
topic: Why you tend to trust people who look similar to you, explaining in group bias and familiarity.
